name: Online video
title: Why Pseudo.com failed, and when online video became viable
question: Why did early internet TV like Pseudo.com fail, and when did online video become viable?
answer: Pseudo.com (1993) ran internet TV channels in the late 1990s; its parent went bankrupt after the dot-com crash and its assets were sold in 2001. Most US homes were still on dial-up. YouTube (2005) launched as broadband passed 17 lines per 100 people and browser video (Flash) worked without a download; Google bought it in 2006 for $1.65B.
verdict_reason: Broadband passed 17 per 100 in 2005, the year YouTube launched.

constraint.name: Broadband and in-browser video
constraint.detail: Video over dial-up was a postage stamp that buffered; it needed broadband and a player that just worked.

crossing.text: US broadband reaches 17 per 100 (World Bank); Flash video plays in the browser.
